newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pre-trial date fixed for Singapore corruption case.
newsitem.headline: Pre-trial date fixed for Singapore corruption case.

text.p: A Singapore official will appear in court next month for a pre-trial hearing on corruption charges involving at least HK$12 million (US$1.55 million), anti-graft officials said on Friday.
They said Taw Cheng Kong would appear on February 22 for a pre-trial hearing of eight charges arising from investments made through Hong Kong asset management firm Rockefeller & Co (Far East) Ltd.
Taw, a regional manager of the Government of Singapore Investment Corp (GIC), was charged on November 5 with corruption involving at least HK$12 million.
He is charged with receiving bribes from Kevin Lee Kwok-wing, then managing director of Rockefeller & Co, to buy specific shares.
Finance Minister Richard Hu told parliament last month Rockefeller & Co had reported the information.
"The GIC has incurred some loss in its investments made through Rockefeller & Co (Far East) Ltd and is in the process of ascertaining the amount," Hu said in response to queries in parliament.
He declined to say exactly how much money was involved.
Taw, who was suspended by GIC, has not yet been asked to enter a plea. He is currently free on bail.
